key_insight: An LLM-assisted analysis linked changes in trial registry entries to higher odds of primary endpoint positivity, without establishing causation.
clinical_relevance: This trial-transparency research, rather than cancer drug discovery, could help reviewers identify registry changes warranting closer scrutiny.
method: Extract randomized clinical trial records from ClinicalTrials.gov.
Detect changes across successive versions using deterministic text analysis and LLM-assisted classification.
Assess associations with primary endpoint positivity and the timing of changes.
evidence_signal: Primary outcome changes were associated with endpoint positivity (OR 1.91; 95% CI 1.48–2.47), as were arm/intervention changes (OR 2.10; 95% CI 1.62–2.73); associations were weaker for changes occurring exclusively before primary completion.
watch_item: The abstract does not report sample size or LLM classification accuracy, limiting assessment of robustness.
paper_title: An LLM-assisted Pipeline for Identifying ClinicalTrials.gov Registry Changes and Their Association with Primary Endpoint Positivity
